result.summary: This PR hardens how the wallet processes PSBTs returned by an external signer: it merges the signer's response into the original PSBT instead of trusting it wholesale, and rejects responses carrying an unsafe sighash type (NONE or SINGLE). It also rewrites the functional test mock signer to run its own offline node and wallet so it can simulate misbehaving or unusual signers, including MuSig2-style multisig in the future. A separate included commit fixes a bug where combinepsbt drops the sighash type when merging inputs, which could make a valid PSBT unfinalizable depending on argument order.
result.problem: External signer users (hardware wallet owners) currently trust the signer's PSBT response verbatim; a compromised or buggy signer could alter outputs or sign with a sighash type that lets a third party alter the transaction after signing, silently costing the user funds. The old test mock could only replay a canned PSBT, so these attack scenarios were never exercised in CI.

open_concerns: jeanpablojp: a finalized signer response bypasses FindUnsafeSighashType because it reads fields the finalizer clears, so a SIGHASH_NONE signature can slip through as complete and broadcastable.

jeanpablojp: PSBTInput::Merge/PSBTOutput::Merge have no failure path other than GetUniqueID and version mismatch, so a signer returning a differently-versioned but otherwise unmodified PSBT is rejected for the wrong reason; worth a clearer error or a version constraint.

jeanpablojp: FindUnsafeSighashType collects signatures from all inputs before checking, so with mixed ECDSA/taproot inputs a bug in either collection branch is masked by the other; suggests single-input test cases per type.

categories.rationale: P2 because it closes a real fund-safety gap for external-signer (hardware wallet) users: a signer using SIGHASH_NONE/SINGLE could let a third party alter outputs after signing, and merging instead of replacing the PSBT rejects a signer that silently changes the transaction. The included sighash-merge fix ('combinepsbt silently drops the sighash type... making the result depend on the argument order') independently fixes a real finalization bug. Impact is bounded because it only affects external-signer users, and review found the hardening is currently incomplete (finalized responses bypass it), which is a review-state concern rather than a reason to discount the underlying problem's importance.

uncertainties: Whether the finalized-PSBT bypass jeanpablojp found is a fundamental design gap or an easy fix affects how close this PR is to being mergeable, but not its priority.

result.card: This PR hardens external signer PSBT handling in the wallet: it merges (rather than blindly accepts) the signer's PSBT response and rejects responses using unsafe sighash types (NONE/SINGLE) that would let a third party alter a transaction after signing. It also rebuilds the functional test mock to run its own wallet, enabling tests of misbehaving signers, and folds in a fix for combinepsbt silently dropping sighash types depending on argument order. The strongest evidence of importance is fund safety for hardware-wallet users: an unsafe sighash type or a tampered signer response could otherwise let funds be redirected after signing. Review is currently Paused: reviewer jeanpablojp found that a finalized PSBT response evades the new sighash check entirely, and the author has been silent for over a week since that was raised. The PR is based on #36076 (merged) and states it absorbs and supersedes #35358's test scenarios.
